locations.name: Es Vergeret
locations.description: Rustic cliffside terrace restaurant above remote Cala Tuent, in the shadow of Puig Major — paellas, local fish, and one of the great lunch views of the Tramuntana. Jessie Granader's boat-day lunch stop ('a very local restaurant with amazing views' — her charter's suggestion), and also on Sa Foradada's own list of fellow sea-view, boat-accessible restaurants. That's the move: arrive by boat on a charter day. By car it's a long hairpin mountain drive past the Sa Calobra road.

references.note: Listed in Sa Foradada's 'Looking for a Restaurant with sea views?' section — fellow seaside restaurants along the coast, accessible by boat.

locations.name: Es Port
locations.description: Seafood house at the tiny fishing cove of Port de Valldemossa, reached by a dramatic hairpin road down from Valldemossa village — fresh fish and rice dishes right on the water in a settlement of a few stone boathouses. From Sa Foradada's sea-view list, and the most itinerary-compatible of its suggestions: an easy pairing with the Son Moragues olive-estate visit or a Valldemossa afternoon during the Deià leg.

locations.name: Sa Foradada
locations.description: Wood-fired paella cooked on the cliffs at the tip of the Sa Foradada peninsula, below Son Marroig — rice and paella over wood, local fish, salads, local desserts; the paella is the must-order. Access and booking corrected from the official site: the primary arrival is by boat from Port de Sóller (~45 min, disembark at the little pier and climb the steps); the walk down from Son Marroig runs about an hour and the site itself doesn't recommend it — wear real shoes if you take the Ravello-style hike option. And despite earlier 'first-come' intel, the site's reviews say to book: call early in the morning while they're prepping. Still the standout candidate for the Sep 2 afternoon, chained to the Son Marroig sunset above.
locations.address: Diseminado Sa Foradada, 2, 07179 Deià, Illes Balears, Spain

references.note: Open in 2026. Wood-fired rice/paella, local fish and seafood. Primary access by boat from Port de Sóller (~45 min); foot access ~1 h from Son Marroig (site does not recommend it). Booking: 'You have to book, call early morning as they're preparing the food.'

locations.name: Ca'n Lluc
locations.description: The second beach restaurant at Cala Deià — on the same rocks as Ca's Patró March, about 30 meters along the cove. Terrace over the bay, well-reviewed seafood (grilled calamari, tuna steak), and a more relaxed, easier-to-book vibe than its famous neighbor. Surfaced from a Reddit thread about Ca's Patró March reservation difficulty as the same-cove fallback, and independently endorsed by Sa Foradada's own sea-view restaurant list.
